minutes.headline: Conservation Commission continued all three hearings to Dec 2 and ratified a beaver-dam emergency order at Flat Hill.
minutes.summary: The commission continued the Cowry Nature Center ADA parking and trail hearing, the 404 Page Street hearing and the Pearl Street determination to December 2. It ratified an emergency certification for a beaver flow device at Flat Hill Road. It discussed hunting calls, dog and trail-sign plans, unauthorized trails, Hollis Road house readiness and the caretaker job description.

votes.motion: Accept the November 4th meeting minutes as drafted
Continue the Cowry Nature Center ADA parking and trail notice of intent to December 2nd, 2026
Continue the 404 Page Street notice of intent to December 2nd, 2026
Continue the 42 Pearl Street request for determination of applicability to December 2nd, 2026
Ratify the emergency certification at 942 Flat Hill Road for a beaver deceiver

budget_items.what_was_said: The engineer needs town contacts for invoices and cancelled checks so expenses can go to the grant administrator for reimbursement.
A member will check whether funds remain on an existing purchase order for trail materials.
A backup cost for mowing was given per cut and per season, plus an optional back-field cut.
No update because the town is still closing the prior fiscal year.
Caretaker duties were allocated hours with a monthly total that would be deducted from rent. The deduction depends on whether state or federal minimum wage applies.
The prior rental agreement was cited against Zillow comparables, and an appraisal was proposed.

decisions.decision: Dog poop fairy sign approved to proceed, with a second official sign on land use rules to be drafted by the agent.
Commissioners will get out to Lane property to find and close unauthorized trails with area-closed signs, starting immediately.
A member will help the pollinator habitat caretaker remove old fencing Saturday around 9.
Agent to send a letter to the neighbor to remove stumps and logs left on the stone wall at Hollis Road.
Agent to take the caretaker job description to HR and labor counsel before the personnel committee.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission continued the Cowry Nature Center ADA parking and trail hearing to December 2, 2026, by a 5-0 vote.
The commission also continued the 404 Page Street hearing and the 42 Pearl Street determination request to December 2, each by 5-0.
The commission ratified an emergency certification for a beaver deceiver at 942 Flat Hill Road.
Commissioners decided to go out to the Lane property and close unauthorized trails with area-closed signs, starting immediately.
The agent will take the Hollis Road caretaker job description to HR and labor counsel before it goes to the personnel committee.

why_it_matters: The Cowry trail and parking project, the Page Street project and the Pearl Street request are still undecided, so none can go ahead until the commission acts at a later meeting.
The Hollis Road caretaker job and rent offset are still open. Their cost to the town budget, mostly taxes, depends on which minimum wage applies and on rental comparables, and neither is settled.
watch_next: December 2, 2026: the Conservation Commission takes up the three continued hearings again.
The caretaker job description, after review by HR and labor counsel, goes to the personnel committee.
